front.title: Problem Statement and Gap Analysis of Fine-Grained QoS Assurance for 6G Scenarios

abstract.t: The evolution toward 6G introduces demanding applications such as holographic communications, tactile internet, digital twins, and semantic communications, which may require fine-grained, per-packet Quality of Service (QoS) assurance. In these scenarios, 5QI may continue to be useful, but it may also need to be complemented by richer service QoS requirement information. Meanwhile, transport networks have developed powerful QoS technologies including FlexE hard slicing, Deterministic Networking (DetNet), Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN), and SRv6 Traffic Engineering policies, enabling per-packet scheduling precision at microsecond levels. However, several gaps remain. First, while 6G scenarios may require richer service QoS requirement information, current IP transport networks still rely on DSCP as the QoS handling mechanism. This could underutilize many effective fine-grained QoS assurance mechanisms already available in transport networks. Second, transport networks lack service-aware perception of upper-layer application attributes. Third, there is no cross-domain information synchronization mechanism between radio access and transport segments, preventing the formation of an end-to-end, full-link QoS assurance mechanism for 6G. This document provides a gap analysis structured around three core gaps: (1) the potential need to complement 5QI with richer service QoS requirement information for 6G and the potential underutilization of fine-grained transport QoS mechanisms due to continued reliance on DSCP in IP transport; (2) lack of service awareness in transport; and (3) missing cross-domain information exchange for end-to-end 6G full- link QoS assurance.
